notes: §1985:VII.2.3.4 GR1: 'all file control entries in the run unit which reference this file connector must have' the same OPTIONAL phrase, a consistent ASSIGN, RECORD DELIMITER and RESERVE, the same organization and access mode, and 'The same specification for the PADDING CHARACTER clause.' The gap of the prior PARTIAL read is closed (kb/Work PB5069 landed, docs/FILES_DESIGN.md D32): BinderDriver.Bind calls ExternalFileConnectorRules.Check at every edition, which compares each describer's FileEntryIdentity.Segments (OPT, ASSIGN, USING, DELIM, RESERVE, ORG, ACC, ..., PAD, the clause now captured by CapturePadding) with the first describer's and reports COBOL6847; FILE STATUS sameness stays 2023-only. Probed at --std 85 (two programs, one compilation group): (b) entries differing in OPTIONAL, ASSIGN literal, RESERVE 2 against none, organization sequential/relative, access sequential/dynamic (relative) and sequential/random (indexed), a PADDING literal against none, two PADDING literals, and two different external PADDING data items each give COBOL6847; (e) RESERVE 1 AREA against none, ACCESS SEQUENTIAL against none, RECORD DELIMITER STANDARD-1 against none (COBOL1778 warning, the declined clause) and two dynamic indexed entries agree and run, and different FILE STATUS items (a 2023-only item) run. Two separately compiled programs whose entries differ in organization end the run with an unhandled System.InvalidOperationException (FileRegistry.SetRelativeKey); 85 defines no detection here, and §1985:I.1.6 says 'The results of violating the formats or rules of Standard COBOL are undefined', so this is not a breach of the rule, though the message's 'the binder screens this' is wrong for that case. The witness runs two agreeing entries and reads back the record the called program wrote. History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read PARTIAL, naming kb/Work PB5069 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5069 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-09.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-09-refute.json).

next.reason: 1985 lists a-g for every file control entry of an external file connector: OPTIONAL, consistent ASSIGN, consistent RECORD DELIMITER, RESERVE, organization, access mode, and 'g. The same specification for the PADDING CHARACTER clause.' §2023:12.4.5.3 GR1 keeps a)-f) (c) now 'Either the STANDARD-1 phrase or a consistent value of feature-name-1') with the implementor's consistency rules documented (§2023:A.1 'FILE-CONTROL entry, ASSIGN clause (consistency rules for external file connectors)' and the RECORD DELIMITER item), drops the PADDING CHARACTER item (the clause is gone from 2023), and adds items no 1985 rule required, among them i) 'The same specification of the FILE STATUS clause, where data-name-4 shall reference the same corresponding external data item'. A 1985 run unit whose sequential entries for one external file name different FILE STATUS items no longer conforms: stricter.
